title: Against Celsus, Book I
blurb: Origen answers Celsus’s opening charges: that Christians meet in secret against the law, that their teaching is barbarian and borrowed, and that they ask for faith without reasons. He then answers the Jew whom Celsus sets against Jesus, meeting the slander about Jesus’ birth and the charge of magic with the prophecies of the virgin, of Bethlehem and of the suffering Servant, and with the lives Jesus changed.
first_english_note: Earlier English: Frederick Crombie (Ante-Nicene Fathers, 1872) and Henry Chadwick (1953). This is a fresh English translation from Koetschau's Greek; neither was used as wording.

text_history.method: Copy-text: Paul Koetschau's edition, GCS 2–3 (Leipzig, 1899), read in the Perseus Digital Library TEI. The English is translated from that Greek, chapter by chapter, and each chapter was then checked clause by clause against the Greek. Koetschau's supplements are followed.
